items.claim: The Song.2.3|2.4 opening cut carries no tier-1 in-verse marker, an undisclosed apple-token link straddles that same seam, and the row's no-addressee ground is contradicted by the imperatives in its own middle verse.
items.evidence: Both sides of the cut are the same first-person voice with a third-masculine-singular subject acting on her: בְּצִלּוֹ֙ חִמַּ֣דְתִּי וְיָשַׁ֔בְתִּי (oshb:Song.2.3, tier: byte) and הֱבִיאַ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Song.2.4, tier: byte); no gendered vocative, no suffix flip and no address-vocabulary anchor sits AT the cut, so the boundary rests on the ABSENCE of an anchor plus a topic change, which is not tier-1 voice-shift evidence. Undisclosed cross-seam token straddling the row's own opening seam: כְּתַפּ֨וּחַ֙ (oshb:Song.2.3, tier: byte) and בַּתַּפּוּחִ֑ים (oshb:Song.2.5, tier: byte) share the tappuach stem (skeleton sweep: 4 verses -- MT 2:3, MT 2:5, MT 7:9 = WEB 7:8, MT 8:5), two of the four sites lying on opposite sides of this cut, and both witnesses carry the link. The no-addressee ground is byte-false inside the span: סַמְּכ֨וּנִי֙ בָּֽאֲשִׁישׁ֔וֹת רַפְּד֖וּנִי בַּתַּפּוּחִ֑ים (oshb:Song.2.5, tier: byte) is two plural imperatives with first-person-singular object suffixes, an explicit addressee -- and the same plural-imperative feature is treated as a boundary driver at MT 2:15 elsewhere in this cluster, so the criterion is applied inconsistently. The closing seam is argued only from an English rendering; the Hebrew וִימִינ֖וֹ תְּחַבְּקֵֽנִי (oshb:Song.2.6, tier: byte) recurs at MT 8:3 at skeleton tier (skeleton sweep of that colon: 2 verses -- MT 2:6, MT 8:3; the verse's left-hand colon differs by one prefixed preposition and so sweeps to 1 verse, which is how the pair escapes an exact sweep), standing directly before the MT 8:4 adjuration, so the embrace-line-plus-adjuration pairing that argues the rival 2:6|2:7 cut is undisclosed. Verified correct: the ahavah-noun object at 10 verses is the right role-split (skeleton sweep of the consonantal string: 15 verses, minus the 5 relative-verb verses MT 1:7 and MT 3:1-3:4); no parashah mark falls in MT 2:4-2:6 and no K/Q note is in span.

items.claim: Every quoted run re-collates at byte tier in MT 2:7, the four-site oath object and FULL-shape identification are byte-correct, and the byte-identity statement against MT 3:5 verifies exactly.
items.evidence: All three quoted runs re-collate at byte tier against oshb:Song.2.7, re-spliced independently from source: the adjuration opener with the daughters vocative הִשְׁבַּ֨עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֜ם בְּנ֤וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ and the doubled adjuration verb אִם תָּעִ֧ירוּ וְֽאִם תְּעֽוֹרְר֛וּ (oshb:Song.2.7, tier: byte), together with the gazelle clause. MT 2:7 and MT 3:5 are character-for-character identical across the whole verse (160 characters, tier: byte), so the row's byte-identity statement is exact rather than approximate, and the three attested adjuration shapes are not harmonized. The oath object is right: skeleton sweep of the adjuration verb = 4 verses (MT 2:7, 3:5, 5:8, 8:4), correctly excluding the daughters' quoted-back form at MT 5:9 (same root, different speech role) -- and no seven or sated reading is imported, the root being oath-only in this book. The FULL shape's two distinguishing members are both present in these bytes, which is what separates this site from the MT 5:8 and MT 8:4 variants. Disclosure hygiene holds: the setumah at MT 2:7 is named as single-witness tier-3 corroboration and explicitly denied driver status; MT 2:7 is not K/Q-bearing (inventory MT 1:17, 2:11, 2:13, 4:9); no special-letter, selah or divine-name claim appears anywhere in the row. Two available strengtheners are noted without being defects: this verse carries one paseq seg (count-only, single-witness), and the rival cut the row rejects has byte support of its own -- the preceding verse's right-hand-embrace colon recurs at MT 8:3 at skeleton tier immediately before the MT 8:4 adjuration, so the rejected alternative could be answered on bytes rather than on assertion.

items.claim: The qol-dodi recurrence is asserted with no tier label and is not byte tier at its second site, and the row's closing verse carries a byte-attested colon that brackets MT 2:8-2:17 across the row's own seam undisclosed.
items.evidence: ק֣וֹל דּוֹדִ֔י re-collates byte at oshb:Song.2.8, but that same pointed run reaches only accent_stripped tier at oshb:Song.5.2, whose attested shape is ק֣וֹל דּוֹדִ֣י דוֹפֵ֗ק (oshb:Song.5.2, tier: byte). The two-site object is therefore skeleton/accent tier (skeleton sweep: 2 verses -- MT 2:8, MT 5:2), and the recurrence claim carries no tier at all, which the tier-disclosure standard requires at write time. Undisclosed cross-seam device: the row's closing verse reads דּוֹמֶ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ לִצְבִ֔י א֖וֹ לְעֹ֣פֶר הָֽאַיָּלִ֑ים (oshb:Song.2.9, tier: byte), and MT 2:17 reads לִצְבִ֗י א֛וֹ לְעֹ֥פֶר הָאַיָּלִ֖ים (oshb:Song.2.17, tier: byte); the shared 19-character consonantal run is a skeleton sweep of 3 verses (MT 2:9, MT 2:17, MT 8:14), and the two Song-2 members sit on opposite sides of this row's closing seam, bracketing MT 2:8-2:17 as one movement. No row in that stretch discloses the bracket. The likeness root compounds the miss through a spelling split -- written with vav at MT 2:9 and without it at MT 2:17 and MT 8:14 (skeleton sweep of the vav-less spelling: 2 verses) -- so an exact sweep of either spelling hides one member of the pair. Verified correct: the closing driver עָנָ֥ה דוֹדִ֖י וְאָ֣מַר לִ֑י (oshb:Song.2.10, tier: byte) is a genuine tier-1 frame verb introducing quoted speech, the two-verse span holds one voice, and the span carries no parashah mark and no K/Q note.

items.claim: The second-feminine-singular marker case is the cluster's strongest and its disclosure symmetry is complete, but the frame-verb wording attributed to the WEB ref is not that witness's rendering, and the blossom-token chain straddling the closing seam is undisclosed.
items.evidence: Byte-solid core: the opening vocative pair re-collates byte at oshb:Song.2.10 and the dove vocative byte at oshb:Song.2.14, and the feminine addressee is visible in the pointed bytes across the span -- הַרְאִ֨ינִי֙ אֶתּ מַרְאַ֔יִךְ (oshb:Song.2.14, tier: byte) carries the feminine suffix kaf-plus-sheva, contrasting byte-visibly with the masculine kaf-plus-qamats at MT 2:17; his address word for her recurs inside the span (skeleton sweep: 9 verses, including MT 2:10 and MT 2:13). Disclosure symmetry is complete: both K/Q-bearing verses in span (MT 2:11, MT 2:13) and both setumah verses in span (MT 2:13, MT 2:14) are named, and no slice crosses the ketiv word standing inside the MT 2:13 refrain. Defect: the frame verb is given as my-beloved-answered-and-said-to-me and attributed to web:Song.2.10, but that witness reads “My beloved spoke, and said to me,” -- the wording ascribed to the cited witness is not its wording. The Hebrew עָנָ֥ה דוֹדִ֖י וְאָ֣מַר לִ֑י (oshb:Song.2.10, tier: byte) does support the answered-gloss, but it is quoted in a different row, not here, so this row's own frame-verb ground is translation-dependent. No English in this row -- or anywhere in this cluster -- is curly-quoted, so the verbatim gate saw zero quotes and could not catch it. Defect: cross-seam cohesion undisclosed at the row's closing seam -- וְהַגְּפָנִ֥ים סְמָדַ֖ר (oshb:Song.2.13, tier: byte) and וּכְרָמֵ֖ינוּ סְמָדַֽר (oshb:Song.2.15, tier: byte) are two of the three book-wide blossom-token sites (skeleton sweep: 3 verses -- MT 2:13, MT 2:15, MT 7:13 = WEB 7:12), sitting on opposite sides of the 2:14|2:15 cut, and both witnesses render the link.

items.claim: Isolating MT 2:15 as its own unit is contested by a byte-attested blossom-and-vineyard chain that straddles the row's own opening seam and is nowhere disclosed.
items.evidence: וּכְרָמֵ֖ינוּ סְמָדַֽר (oshb:Song.2.15, tier: byte) shares its blossom token with וְהַגְּפָנִ֥ים סְמָדַ֖ר (oshb:Song.2.13, tier: byte); the skeleton sweep of that token returns 3 verses book-wide (MT 2:13, MT 2:15, MT 7:13 = WEB 7:12), so two of the three sites sit two verses apart across this row's own opening seam, and both witnesses carry the link. Under the cross-seam standard a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed, and that disclosure is exactly what a single-verse isolation held at low confidence most needs. The vineyard family in the same verse is a second, weaker strand of the same chain and is subject to the allography split (the bare spelling with final mem sweeps to 1 verse, MT 8:11, while the suffixed spellings standing in this verse escape that sweep) -- name the attested spelling before any vineyard digit is used in either direction. The row's positive grounds are byte-true as far as they go: the quoted imperative clause re-collates byte at oshb:Song.2.15; the imperative and the two first-person-plural forms mark an addressee and a speaking group but no speaker gender; and no dodi, no his-word-for-her and no daughters vocative stands in the verse (the next address anchor is דּוֹדִ֥י לִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י ל֔וֹ at oshb:Song.2.16, tier: byte). Held, not asserted: the gender of the plural imperative cannot be settled from the staged extract, which carries no morphology layer, and both witnesses' renderings are gender-neutral there -- so it is counted neither for nor against the isolation. No parashah mark and no K/Q note falls in this one-verse span.

items.claim: The stated ground of no addressee or gender-marked interruption is contradicted by MT 2:17's own bytes, which carry two imperatives and a masculine-singular suffix that MT 2:16 lacks, and the gazelle-and-fawn bracket reaching back to MT 2:9 is undisclosed.
items.evidence: סֹב֩ דְּמֵה לְךָ֨ דוֹדִ֜י (oshb:Song.2.17, tier: byte) turns to direct address: the suffix is kaf-plus-qamats, the masculine-singular form, contrasting byte-visibly with the feminine kaf-plus-sheva of הַרְאִ֨ינִי֙ אֶתּ מַרְאַ֔יִךְ (oshb:Song.2.14, tier: byte), and both witnesses render the clause as address to the male beloved. MT 2:16 has no addressee at all -- דּוֹדִ֥י לִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י ל֔וֹ with הָרֹעֶ֖ה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים (oshb:Song.2.16, tier: byte) is third-person reference throughout. A gender-marked addressee therefore IS introduced at the 2:16|2:17 junction; the row denies the interruption in one clause and cites the very imperative that makes it in the next, and the same feature is used as a cut driver at MT 2:15 elsewhere in this cluster. The unit may still stand on single-speaker continuity, but continuity alone is tier-2 corroboration, not the tier-1 ground the row states. Undisclosed bracket: לִצְבִ֗י א֛וֹ לְעֹ֥פֶר הָאַיָּלִ֖ים (oshb:Song.2.17, tier: byte) shares a 19-character consonantal run with MT 2:9 and MT 8:14 (skeleton sweep: 3 verses); the MT 2:9 and MT 2:17 members bracket MT 2:8-2:17 across three of this cluster's seams, and no row in the stretch discloses it. Tier omission, cured cheaply: the day-cooling recurrence claim carries no tier though the strongest one is available -- עַ֤ד שֶׁיָּפ֨וּחַ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וְנָ֖סוּ הַצְּלָלִ֑ים is character-identical at oshb:Song.2.17 and oshb:Song.4.6 (tier: byte at both). Verified correct: the mutual-belonging shape is quoted in the attested his-mine order rather than harmonized with the flipped MT 6:3 shape or the desire variant at MT 7:11 = WEB 7:10; the setumah at MT 2:17 is disclosed as single-witness tier-3 corroboration; and the grazing participle in MT 2:16 is the graze member of the resh-ayin family, not the address word, which the row does not blend.

items.claim: The driver asserts the seek-formula recurs verbatim at three further sites at tier byte each, but re-collation returns accent_stripped at MT 3:3, and the narrated-past-tense characterization that carries the unit type is contradicted by the bytes at three points.
items.evidence: The formula as spliced from its first site, שֶׁאָהֲבָ֖ה נַפְשִׁ֑י (oshb:Song.3.1, tier: byte), re-collates byte at oshb:Song.3.2 and oshb:Song.3.4 but only accent_stripped at oshb:Song.3.3, whose attested pointing is שֶׁאָהֲבָ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֖י (oshb:Song.3.3, tier: byte); the reverse test agrees, the MT 3:3 form reaching only accent_stripped at MT 3:1. The stated tier-byte-each is therefore machine-refuted at one of the three cited sites, and a verbatim claim is quotation-grade only where byte tier is proven. The honest object is a 5-verse skeleton-tier formula (skeleton sweep: MT 1:7, 3:1, 3:2, 3:3, 3:4), four of them in this span -- and the MT 1:7 site outside the span is what makes both the tier and the scope worth naming. The verb-form characterization is contradicted by the pointed bytes: אָק֨וּמָה נָּ֜א וַאֲסוֹבְבָ֣ה בָעִ֗יר and אֲבַקְשָׁ֕ה (oshb:Song.3.2, tier: byte) are prefix-conjugation forms carrying a final he, the first reinforced by the entreaty particle standing beside it, and the other witness reads them as volitives rather than as narration; אַרְפֶּ֔נּוּ (oshb:Song.3.4, tier: byte) is likewise not a suffix-conjugation form; and רְאִיתֶֽם (oshb:Song.3.3, tier: byte) carries the second-person plural ending and is read by both witnesses as a question put to the watchmen named in the same verse, quoted address standing inside a span the row characterizes as an event chain rather than pure address -- which is the ground the unit type rests on. Recasting the chain as narrated past tense overstates what the bytes carry at the rising, the going-about, the seeking, the not-letting-go and the watchmen question. Verified correct: the span carries no parashah mark and no K/Q note (inventory MT 1:17, 2:11, 2:13, 4:9); the four in-span formula sites are real; and the closing seam is byte-grounded, MT 3:5 being character-identical to MT 2:7 across the whole verse, so the adjuration bracket that closes the unit is exactly the attested FULL shape.
